doc.title: Ann Rabson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 21, 2007

title: Unpaid Chicago playing: Job Corps, veterans' hospitals and Richard Pryor
summary: She played for free at the Job Corps and veterans' hospitals, and saw Richard Pryor at his funniest there; she left Chicago in 1971.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Wow. And were you performing — mostly that would have been as a solo performer.

Oh yeah. Most of my career has been solo. I love, as you probably found out, I love playing with other people, but mostly I play by myself. And I did play some in Chicago but I played for nothing. I played for the Job Corps Center, I played for veterans’ hospitals, this was when the Vietnam War was going on and there were a lot of paraplegics, you know I played for them. You know, great audience. But at the Job Corps, I played for the Job Corps one time and there was this young comedian who was also playing there, a guy named Richard Pryor. He was so funny. And I’ve never seen him funnier than he was at that show. I mean never on television, never in the movies, never, nothing. He was so funny and so — I mean he was playing to these Job Corps kids and it was just terrific.
And this would have been the early seventies?
Late sixties. I left Chicago in ’71.
